description_full: Adeia Inc., together with its subsidiaries, operates as a media and semiconductor intellectual property licensing platform company in the United States, Asia, Canada, Europe, the Middle East, and internationally. The company licenses its patent portfolios across various markets, including multichannel video programming distributors comprising cable, satellite, and telecommunications television providers that aggregate and distribute linear content over networks, as well as television providers that aggregate and stream linear content over broadband networks; over-the-top video service providers, such as subscription video-on-demand and free advertising-supported streaming service providers, providers that offer online services and devices that enable internet streaming and downloading of movies, television shows, music and other types of media content, as well as content providers, networks, and media companies. It also licenses consumer electronics manufacturers, which includes producers of smart televisions, streaming media devices, video game consoles, mobile devices, content storage devices, and other connected media devices; semiconductors, including providers of memory, logic, sensors, and radio frequency devices; and social media companies that allow users to stream and upload user-generated content. The company licenses its intellectual properties under the Adeia brand. The company was formerly known as Xperi Holding Corporation and changed its name to Adeia Inc. The company was incorporated in 2019 and is headquartered in San Jose, California.

financial_summary: Adeia Inc. is a small-cap technology business with a $1.8B market cap on $443M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +0% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory. Operating margins are expanding by +3.9pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 13% against a 9% cost of capital, a 3-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it.

The business throws off $156M in free cash flow — roughly 35 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.42× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.6× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 4.3×.

Shareholder yield of 2.4% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 1.7× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 39% operating margin runs 33pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.

Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-14.6% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 533 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 78% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 42% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 53% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 68% and a beta of 1.02, it moves roughly with the market.
About $24.0M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 45% in the 2020 crash, 30% in the 2022 bear market and 80% in 2008.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $7.70 (margin of safety -111%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 37%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $5.00 to $11.69 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Technology peers: P/E 15.7 vs 27.4, EV/EBITDA 7.8 vs 17.1 and P/FCF 11.5 vs 26.1 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 2% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are attractive: an FCF yield of 8.7% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 8.3% (vs the 8% bar).
The 4 covering analysts target $38.25 on average, 136% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 13% earns above the cost of capital of 9.2%, but the 3pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.54).
It converts 35% of revenue into free cash flow, or 27% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 7/9 and cash conversion of 1.42x.
ROE of 23% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.2x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 12pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 15.2% of revenue on R&D and 7.8% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: Leverage is moderate at 1.6x net debt to EBITDA ($136.7M of cash against $418.5M of debt), above the 1.5x gate, with interest covered 4.3x.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 0.3% over 3 years and -13.0% over 5 years, so growth is accelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 22%).
At current returns, reinvesting 28% of profits supports about 3.6% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded -17.9% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 0.88 (orders lagging sales), a backlog worth 98% of annual revenue and deferred revenue down 17%.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (0.9x, 0.4% of sales), a maintenance pace.
own: Insiders own a modest 2.0%, and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
It returns 2.4% a year to shareholders (1.2% in buybacks and 1.2% in dividends).
The share count has grown 1.3% a year over five years, diluting existing holders.
It has paid a dividend for 13 consecutive years, though it has been cut 6.7% a year over the last five.
Short interest is elevated at 11.1% of the float, 5.8 days to cover.
people: With about 155 employees, each generates about $2.9M of revenue, 7.7x the Technology median, and revenue has fallen 13.0% a year across its filed history.
